name: Lactoferrin
short: Trials in anaemic children found constipation, vomiting and abdominal pain (less constipation with lactoferrin). Reviews: no adverse effects in preterm infants, fewer H. pylori therapy side effects.
text: In a systematic review of twelve randomised trials of lactoferrin added to the feeds of preterm infants, the investigators reported no adverse effects in the included studies, and there was no difference in death from any cause (11 studies, 5510 infants, moderate-certainty evidence); most other findings were of low certainty. A systematic review of 11 trials in children with iron-deficiency anaemia, whose abstract describes groups given lactoferrin alone or with iron being compared with iron alone or placebo, found that adverse events such as constipation, vomiting, loss of appetite and abdominal pain occurred, with a significant decrease in constipation in the lactoferrin-treated groups; the abstract does not say which groups the other events occurred in, does not name the comparison group for constipation and does not give the number of events in each group. In a meta-analysis of nine randomised trials (1343 patients) comparing lactoferrin with placebo or no treatment during Helicobacter pylori eradication treatment, total side effects occurred in 9.05% of the groups given lactoferrin and 16.28% of the groups not given it; the authors describe these as side effects related to the H. pylori treatment. These trials cover specific groups and settings, and the abstracts do not report on long-term use in healthy adults. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
